A.explanation: Too small by a factor of 1000. It uses microseconds instead of milliseconds from the $5 \text{ ms cm}^{-1}$ time-base.

B.explanation: Too small by a factor of 1000. It correctly divides total time by 3.5 cycles but converts $\text{ms}$ to $\text{s}$ incorrectly.

C.explanation: Half the correct period. It assumes $7$ half-cycles in $10.0 \text{ cm}$ are $7$ full periods instead of $3.5$ full periods.

D.explanation: Total time $50 \text{ ms}$ divided by $3.5$ complete cycles gives about $14 \text{ ms} = 1.4 \times 10^{-2} \text{ s}$.

hints: Notice the horizontal scale: $10.0 \text{ cm}$ at $5 \text{ ms cm}^{-1}$ means the whole trace represents $50 \text{ ms}$, not the period itself.
Count complete sine cycles across the $10.0 \text{ cm}$ trace using peaks and troughs: there are 4 peaks but only 3 troughs, so it is not 3 or 4 full waves.
Connect total time to one cycle with $T = \text{total time} / \text{number of cycles}$, then convert $\text{ms}$ to $\text{s}$ for the final period.
walkthrough: Identify the horizontal time information: time-base $= 5 \text{ ms cm}^{-1}$ and trace width $= 10.0 \text{ cm}$.
Calculate the total time displayed: $t = 10.0 \times 5 = 50 \text{ ms}$.
Count the number of full cycles in that width. The trace starts mid-way rising and ends mid-way falling, with 4 crests and 3 troughs, which is $3.5$ complete sine waves.
Apply the period rule $T = t / N$: $T = 50 \text{ ms} / 3.5 \approx 14.3 \text{ ms}$.
Convert to seconds: $14.3 \text{ ms} = 14.3 \times 10^{-3} \text{ s} \approx 1.4 \times 10^{-2} \text{ s}$. This is option D.
